metadata.notes: Path C — Social Engineering of Human Operator. Scenario: LegitimateAgentCompromised (Layer 2 AI-Specific). Human is manipulated into instructing the agent to perform actions counter to security interests. Classic #9 (Social Engineering) enabling #1 (Abuse of Functions). Notation: #9 ||[human][@External→@Org]|| →[Δt=?] #1 + [DRE: C, I]. Delta_t between steps is variable (hours to days — depends on human response time). Velocity: VC-1 to VC-2 (human-dependent gap), then VC-4 (agent execution). The #9→#1 transition has a human-speed gap where awareness training and verification procedures are viable. Once the human issues the instruction, agent execution is VC-4. Source: 'Agentic AI Under the Microscope — Why AI Security Is Not a Threat Category' (Bernhard Kreinz, 2026-02-25).

path_sequence.notes: Attacker manipulates human operator via social engineering (phishing, pretexting, authority impersonation). Generic vulnerability: human psychological factors (trust, authority bias, urgency). Delta_t is variable: hours to days depending on human response time.

Manipulated human instructs agent to perform actions (data export, configuration change, communication). Generic vulnerability: scope and trust in agent's legitimate functions, now directed by a manipulated operator.
